title: observability-token-kv-cost-latency-dashboard-alert-refinements
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Context: We recently observed noisy paging alerts and asymmetric cost attribution for requests hitting the KV cache. This PR refines token-level KV cost and latency metrics, tightens alert thresholds, and updates dashboards to make signal-to-noise better for SRE and platform teams. Motivation: reduce pager fatigue from transient cache misses and make it easier to correlate token-level cost spikes with specific model routes and cache hit ratios.

What this PR does:
- Adds a token_cost_aggregator service that computes per-request token cost broken down by compute vs KV fetchs and tags by model, route, and plan.
- Emits new metrics: redwood.kv.tokens.fetched, redwood.kv.tokens.charge, redwood.kv.latency.p50/p90/p99, and redwood.kv.cache_hit_ratio with consistent labels.
- Enhances tracing to add kv.fetch.span with attributes for key_shard and fetch_size.
- Updates Dashboards (token_kv_cost) with cost/latency breakdown panels and a new aggregated heatmap for high-cost routes.
- Refines alerting rules: introduce a 10m sustained signal for cost-per-token regression, require cache_hit_ratio < 0.85 combined with p99 latency > 150ms before firing.
- Adds docs and runbook snippets for SRE on investigating token-level cost spikes.

Checklist:
- [x] Instrument metrics and traces in token path
- [x] Update dashboards and panel descriptions
- [x] Create alert thresholds and silence default noisy alerts
- [x] Add integration tests that simulate KV miss storms and validate metrics semantics
- [x] Add runbook and cross-team notes

Testing:
- Unit tests for aggregator logic and label normalization added.
- Integration test (observability_test.go) simulates burst of requests with mixed cache hits/misses and asserts emitted metrics and that alerting rule does not fire for transient spikes.
- Local Grafana dashboard validated against generated test data.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy token_cost_aggregator behind a feature flag (off by default).
2) Gradually enable for 10% of routes for 24 hours; monitor new panels and ensure no false positives.
3) Enable alerting rule in staging for 48 hours then promote to prod.

Related: ENG-4521 (kv cost visibility), ENG-4680 (alert noise reduction).
commits: Add token_cost_aggregator service and aggregator tests
Add kv.fetch tracing span and attributes
Dashboard: add token_kv_cost panels and heatmap
Alerting: refine rules for cost-per-token and cache_hit_ratio
Integration test: observability_test.go to simulate KV miss storm
review_comments: Liam Chen: Can you add cardinality guidance for labels? Token-level labels can blow up metrics ingestion costs.
Ava Martinez: Added normalization and cardinality guidance section in token_cost_aggregator.go and docs. Labels limited to model, route, plan, region.
Priya Kapoor: Alert looks good but recommend requiring sustained signal across two regions before paging.
Ava Martinez: Updated alert rule to require cross-region confirmation (or default to single-region with louder threshold) — documented in runbook.
Marco Ruiz: Integration test flake observed on first run (race); suggest small delay in test harness.
Ava Martinez: Fixed race by adding deterministic ordering and retry in test harness; CI now passes.
release_notes: Refined token-level KV cost & latency observability: new metrics (redwood.kv.tokens.*, redwood.kv.latency.*), improved dashboards (token_kv_cost), and tuned alerting rules to reduce noise. No breaking changes. Rollout behind feature flag.
notes: This PR reduces alert noise by combining cache_hit_ratio and p99 latency conditions; SRE requested follow-up to expose per-tenant rate-limits on emitted metrics if ingestion costs grow.
